what_it_does: LiDAR-inertial odometry is the problem of figuring out where a robot or self-driving car is by combining a laser scanner (LiDAR) with motion sensors (an inertial measurement unit, or IMU). Two existing families of algorithms trade off differently: filter-based methods update an estimate incrementally and are fast but accumulate error over time; graph-based methods revisit past poses to correct errors but are computationally expensive. LIO-DPC proposes a hybrid: a fast filter produces an initial pose estimate, and then a lightweight local graph optimizer corrects it by chaining together only nearby recent poses rather than the full history. A loop-closing step further reduces drift by selectively picking representative loops — avoiding the cost of processing every possible loop closure — based on how close they are in both time and space. The claimed result is accuracy comparable to full graph optimization at a speed closer to filter-based methods.
